title: Nonzero pencil differential gives a finite surjective generically etale map
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and let $s,t\in\Gamma(C,M)$ generate $M$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Let $h=[s:t]:C	o\mathbf P^1_F$ be their morphism [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections]. In local frames write $s=\alpha e,t= eta e$ and let $\delta(s,t)$ be the global section of $\Omega^1_{C/F}\otimes M^{\otimes2}$ defined by $( eta\,d\alpha-\alpha\,d eta)e^{\otimes2}$, with the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], Kähler derivation and tensor product as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The target $\mathbf P^1_F$ is a smooth separated integral curve of dimension one. On the open $t
e0$ the pullback of an affine target coordinate is $s/t$ and $d(s/t)=( eta\,d\alpha-\alpha\,d eta)/ eta^2$; the analogous formula on $s
e0$ gives $dh
e0$ [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map] if and only if $\delta(s,t)
e0$. If $\delta(s,t)
e0$, then $h$ is finite, surjective, and etale on a nonempty open of $C$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Furthermore, for an algebraic closure $K/F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $\delta(s_K,t_K)
e0$, both $s_K,t_K$ are nonzero sections, and the rational function $r=h_K^*z\in K(C_K)$ for the standard affine coordinate $z$ has $dr
e0$, is not in $K$, and defines exactly $h_K$ by the smooth proper curve/function-field correspondence [def-sc-function-field]. The projection $\mathbf P^1_K	o\mathbf P^1_F$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, so finiteness of $h_K$ descends to $h$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-pc-base-change]. No perfection or characteristic hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

proof.text: For any field $E$, the standard cover of $P=\mathbf P^1_E$ consists of $\operatorname{Spec}E[z]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}E[w]$, with overlap $\operatorname{Spec}E[z,z^{-1}]$ and $w=z^{-1}$. Each chart is smooth of relative dimension one by the affine-space lemma, so $P$ is smooth of dimension one. Both chart rings are domains and the overlap is nonempty and dense in each; hence $P$ is reduced and irreducible, and is integral. Explicitly the prime chains in $E[z]$ have length at most one since every nonzero prime is generated by an irreducible polynomial, and $(0)\subset(z)$ has length one. The projective-space properness lemma makes $P$ proper, in particular separated and of finite type. This proves the asserted target geometry for $E=F$ and later for $E=K$.

source.place: Tag 0B2P, lemma-projective-space-smooth, n=1; constructions.tex Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space

proof.text: Change a local frame from $e$ to $e'=u e$, where $u$ is a unit. Then $\alpha'=u^{-1}\alpha$, $\beta'=u^{-1}\beta$ and the Leibniz rule gives $\beta' d\alpha'-\alpha' d\beta'=u^{-2}(\beta d\alpha-\alpha d\beta)$: the two terms involving $du$ cancel. Thus the displayed local tensors glue to $\delta(s,t)$. The projective-space section construction and chart lemma identify $h^{-1}(D_+(T_1))$ with the open $t\ne0$ and $h^*(T_0/T_1)=\alpha/\beta$ there. Differentiating $\beta\cdot\beta^{-1}=1$ gives $d(\alpha/\beta)=\beta^{-2}(\beta d\alpha-\alpha d\beta)$. On $s\ne0$ the other coordinate has derivative $d(\beta/\alpha)=-\alpha^{-2}(\beta d\alpha-\alpha d\beta)$. These opens cover because $s,t$ generate. On each target affine line its differential module is free on the coordinate differential (a derivation of $E[z]$ is uniquely determined by its value on $z$); the definition of $dh$ therefore identifies it with these derivatives. Consequently $dh=0$ exactly when $\delta(s,t)=0$.

source.place: Tags 01NE, lemma-projective-space, and 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space; morphisms.tex Tag 01UV, lemma-functoriality-differentials; explicit agent frame/quotient calculation

proof.text: Assume $\delta(s,t)\ne0$. The preceding calculation gives $dh\ne0$. The smooth-curve differential criterion applies to $h:C\to\mathbf P^1_F$: both schemes are separated integral finite-type smooth schemes of dimension one. It supplies a nonempty open $V\subseteq C$ with $h|_V$ étale. This already proves the generic étaleness over the original field $F$.

The projectivity assumption on $C$ supplies a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_F$ whose composite with the structural projection is its structure morphism. The projection is proper, a closed immersion is proper, and composites of proper morphisms are proper. Thus $C$ is proper over $F$.

Fix an algebraic closure $K/F$ and set $D=C_K$. Since $C$ is geometrically integral, $D$ is integral and nonempty. Apply the smooth-curve cotangent lemma with $X=Y=C$ and $h=\mathrm{id}_C$; its hypotheses hold because $C$ is smooth, integral, finite type and dimension one, and is separated by step 4. It says that the structure morphism of $C$ has relative dimension one. Smoothness of relative dimension one survives base change, so $D$ is smooth of dimension one over $K$; properness also survives base change. In particular $D$ is a smooth proper integral finite-type $K$-curve. Projective space commutes with base change, so the geometric target is exactly $\mathbf P^1_K$.

source.place: Tags 01VB, lemma-base-change-smooth, 02NK, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d, and 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper; varieties.tex definition-geometrically-integral

proof.text: Pull back $M,s,t$ to $D$. Local frames pull back to frames and a local relation generating $M$ pulls back to the same relation, so $s_K,t_K$ generate $M_K$. The functor-of-points construction commutes with pullback, hence $[s_K:t_K]=h_K$. The relative differential base-change isomorphism sends $1\otimes da$ to $d(1\otimes a)$, so it sends the pulled-back tensor $\delta(s,t)$ to $\delta(s_K,t_K)$. To check nonvanishing without assuming a global-sections base-change theorem, choose an affine frame open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ where the local representative $\omega\in\Omega_{A/F}$ of $\delta$ is nonzero. On $U_K$ the representative is $1\otimes\omega\in K\otimes_F\Omega_{A/F}$. Extend $1\in K$ to an $F$-basis, or choose an $F$-linear functional $\lambda:K\to F$ with $\lambda(1)=1$; then $\lambda\otimes1$ retracts this inclusion. Thus $1\otimes\omega\ne0$ and $\delta(s_K,t_K)\ne0$.

proof.text:
Neither $s_K$ nor $t_K$ is the zero section, since either equality would make the local expression for $\delta(s_K,t_K)$ zero. The nonvanishing open of $t_K$ is nonempty: on an integral scheme a nonzero section of a line bundle has nonzero generic germ, since in a frame this is the injection of a domain into its fraction field. It contains the generic point $\eta$ of $D$, and $r=h_K^*z=s_K/t_K$ is a rational function. The ratio calculation gives $dh_K
e0$. The cotangent generic-isomorphism lemma makes $(dh_K)_\eta$ nonzero. Over the $t_K$ chart the generator $dz$ maps to $dr$, and localization of Kähler differentials identifies this stalk calculation with differentiation in $K(D)$. Therefore $dr
e0$. As $d$ kills $K$, $r
otin K$. In particular $h_K$ cannot factor through a $K$-rational point: the point at infinity would force $t_K=0$, and any affine point would force $r$ to be constant.

proof.text: Apply the proper-curve/function-field correspondence over the algebraically closed field $K$ to $h_K$. Its nonconstancy was just proved, and both curves are smooth proper integral. It follows that $h_K$ sends the generic point to the generic point and induces the field embedding $K(\mathbf P^1)\hookrightarrow K(D)$. On the affine coordinate $z$ this embedding is $z\mapsto r$ by the ratio computation. A $K$-embedding from $K(z)$ is determined by the image of $z$: every rational function $a(z)/b(z)$ maps to $a(r)/b(r)$. The correspondence is a bijection on these morphisms, so the embedding $z\mapsto r$ defines exactly $h_K$, proving the requested identification rather than merely producing some curve map from $r$.

source.place: Tag 0BY1, theorem-curves-rational-maps, fully faithful functor and identification of the map on the function field

proof.text: The proper-over-separated lemma makes $h_K$ proper, since $D$ is proper over $K$ and $\mathbf P^1_K$ is separated. Its image is closed and contains the generic point by the preceding step, so it is all of the integral target. In particular the image of the sole irreducible component $D$ contains at least two points (for example $0$ and infinity). Apply the proper dimension-one noncontraction lemma to $X=D$, $Y=\mathbf P^1_K$, $f=h_K$: $X$ is proper of dimension one, $Y$ is separated, and the unique curve component is not contracted. This proves that $h_K$ is finite as well as surjective.

Write $q:\mathbf P^1_K\to\mathbf P^1_F$ for the base-change projection. On either standard affine chart it is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_F K)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A=F[z]$ or $F[w]$. These ring maps are faithfully flat by the field-extension base-change lemma. A faithfully flat map is flat, and the affine flatness criterion therefore proves flatness of $q$ on this cover. Surjectivity on each chart follows from surjectivity on prime spectra for faithfully flat maps; hence $q$ is surjective. Finally $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is quasi-compact and quasi-compactness survives base change; since $q$ is precisely that base change, $q$ is quasi-compact. No finite-degree assumption on $K/F$ has been used.

source.place: Tags 00HI, lemma-flat-base-change, and 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings; schemes.tex Tags 01K4, lemma-quasi-compact-affine, and 01K5, lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change

proof.text: The square with $h_K$ and $h$ is the base-change square along $q$, by the projective-space base-change identification and the pullback compatibility checked above. As $q$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, finiteness of $h_K$ descends to finiteness of $h$. For surjectivity, given $y\in\mathbf P^1_F$, lift it to $y_K$ using surjectivity of $q$, then lift $y_K$ to $x_K\in D$ using surjectivity of $h_K$. The image $x\in C$ satisfies $h(x)=y$ by commutativity. Together with step 3 this proves all three assertions over $F$. The argument used only field-extension faithful flatness and the smooth-curve differential criterion over a field, both valid in every characteristic; it imposed no perfection assumption.
